editorial.headline: Clay and Ceramic Building Materials With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23929 covers non-brick clay and ceramic building materials, open to all business scales and nationally open to foreign ownership.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23929 sits in a practical corner of building-materials manufacturing: fired clay and ceramic products made for construction, but not ordinary bricks or roof tiles. Its scope includes drainage channels, floor and wall tiles, ventilation blocks, well rings, ceramic furnaces, mosaic cubes, paving and non-refractory ceramic tiles, chimney elements, pipes, ceramic conduits, roof tiles, and fired-clay floor blocks. In plain English, this is the industrial category for shaped clay or ceramic components that become part of buildings, infrastructure, and site works.

The activity is not limited to a single business scale. The record opens it to **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** operators, which matters because this line can range from smaller specialist production to heavier manufacturing. The common thread is not the size of the factory but the nature of the product: clay or ceramic building materials made as construction inputs. A founder reading this code should therefore focus less on a generic “ceramics” label and more on whether the output is a building-material component within the listed scope.

Nationally, the picture is straightforward. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited national source. That means the national record does not impose a foreign-share cap below full ownership for this activity. There is no basis in the slim record to add a special capital figure, local partner requirement, licensing timeline, or other threshold; the defensible statement is simply that the national foreign-ownership position is open up to the recorded ceiling.

Bali is also not a hidden stop sign here. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA across the island, but the Bali reason for this record says the OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by that moratorium. That does not turn the code into a blank cheque for matters outside the record, but it gives the key registration signal: for this activity, the national openness and the Bali-side moratorium screen point in the same usable direction.
